data_basis: public synthetic sample DB (illustrative; reproducible from bnbhack/data/make_sample_db.py). Figures demonstrate the engine's mechanics and ablation, not a live track record. Sub-year spans report window metrics, not annualised CAGR.
note: Returns are NET of the modelled round-trip cost. Edge stats come only from the train window; the test equity curve is fully out of sample. The engine's value claim rests on the bounded-drawdown property and the edge-gated leg, not on the naive leg failing. The kelly_engine leg (drawdown-budget fractional-Kelly) halts new risk as drawdown approaches the cap, so the hard cap holds by construction. The naive_flat_leverage leg runs the same signals at a constant leverage equal to the engine's realised average (naive_flat_leverage_x); at that small constant size it cannot run to ruin, and over a short window it can post a positive return with a small drawdown, as the figures here show. The kelly_engine_with_edge_gate leg layers a stricter net-of-cost selection on top of Kelly: it only sizes a bucket whose measured per-trade expectancy clears the round-trip cost with a statistical margin. At the live production basis (24h horizon, 0.2 percent V3 round-trip) this overlay lifts net return while the same drawdown cap holds, so it is enabled live; at higher modelled costs it lowers turnover and return for similar drawdown, acting as a conservative risk-tightening filter. The reported figures, not this prose, are the source of truth for the active basis.
